categories.title: Hip mobility and gait
categories.description: Hip osteoarthritis and arthroplasty studies describe changes in hip motion, walking speed, symmetry and movement at adjacent joints.
categories.reading_note: Check the walking speed and which limb was measured. Hip impairment can also affect loading at the knee.

categories.title: Knee mobility and gait
categories.description: Studies of knee osteoarthritis, rehabilitation and replacement report changes in knee angles, joint loading, walking patterns and function.
categories.reading_note: Check whether the result concerns pain, radiographic severity, the knee adduction moment or observed motion. Each outcome needs its own reference.

categories.title: Ankle and foot mobility
categories.description: Ankle osteoarthritis, ankle replacement and foot mobility studies address distal motion, propulsion and compensation during walking.
categories.reading_note: Identify the phase of the gait cycle and the foot and shank landmarks. Forefoot and ankle restrictions can affect similar gait measures.

categories.title: Clinical background and gait assessment
categories.description: Clinical texts, reviews and broader gait studies explain the variables used in assessment and why patterns must be interpreted in context.
categories.reading_note: Use these sources for definitions and measurement choices. Check the joint and comparison group in the relevant primary study.

categories.title: Human action recognition
categories.description: Skeleton and movement representations are used to recognise actions from body landmarks, depth frames or motion sequences.
categories.reading_note: Read the task label and validation protocol before using a recognition result to support a claim about gait or joint angles.

categories.title: Video-based gait and joint measurement
categories.description: Video and depth systems estimate gait timing, spatial measures, joint trajectories and range of motion.
categories.reading_note: Compare like outcomes and views. Check the calibration, units and biomechanical reference for each estimate.

categories.title: Human pose estimation and posture
categories.description: Pose and posture studies describe how images become landmark estimates, 3D representations or movement classifications.
categories.reading_note: Check which joints the system actually detects, how missing landmarks are handled and which outputs were evaluated in people walking.

categories.title: Agreement, repeatability and clinical validation
categories.description: Comparisons with reference systems and repeated measurements help establish when a markerless estimate is reliable in the tested setting.
categories.reading_note: Look at the error in the individual variable and the population used for validation. Detection, agreement and sensitivity to change answer different questions.

categories.title: Occlusion, clothing and illumination
categories.description: These studies test clothing, difficult visibility or lighting, and include pose methods that address ambiguous or crowded scenes.
categories.reading_note: Separate missing anatomical landmarks during swing from lighting and clothing effects. Check whether the same condition was tested in the relevant gait population.

categories.title: Datasets and benchmark methods
categories.description: Dataset and benchmark papers provide examples of the data and protocols used to evaluate gait or skeleton-based recognition methods.
categories.reading_note: Check whether the outcome is an action class, joint position or clinical gait measure, and whether subjects are held out.

categories.title: Gait recognition and biometrics
categories.description: Gait recognition work contributes motion representations and context for distinguishing identification tasks from joint assessment.
categories.reading_note: Read identity recognition as evidence about representations. Check for separate validation before using one to estimate an angle or impairment.

categories.title: Fall-related gait and complementary sensing
categories.description: Video, surface electromyography and related fall-assessment research cover altered gait patterns, functional tests and fall-related endpoints.
categories.reading_note: Check the endpoint and follow-up. Classifying a recorded pattern and predicting future falls call for different evaluation designs.
